newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Telstra and News Corp have agreed to sell their 100 per cent interest in Foxtel in a major breakthrough for rationalisation in the Australian pay-TV industry. In return for the sale, the companies will get a combined majority stake in Australis. The listing of Foxtel is likely to be announced this week, but must still be cleared by the company's bondholders and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission. Page 1.

The underwriters of ICI Australia's A$2.25 billion share offering are expected to exercise their option over the last 12 million shares held by the departing parent company ICI plc. A list of the top 20 shareholders is expected to be unveiled this morning and and it is predicted that a Westpac nominee company will be the largest holder of ICIA shares with four per cent, while the AMP Society is expected to hold about three per cent. Page 19.

The Ten Network has recorded an eight per cent rise in revenue for the nine months to May, but company executives have warned the results for the year to June will not be as positive as the period includes the Seven Network's screening of the Atlanta Olymics last year. Ten's major stakeholder CanWest said its share of profit for the three months to May rose 35.5 per cent to A$32.3 million, boosted by its increased interest in the network. Page 19.

Cash Converters founder Brian Cumins has sold his 30 per cent stake in the second hand goods franchiser for A$14.3 million. Managing director Peter Cumins and legal director Michael Cooke will each take up a third of the stake at 30 cents a share, while the remainder will be purchased by clients of Godfrey Pembroke financial consultants. Cumins will remain as non-executive chairman. Page 21.

The new New South Wales TAB chairman Gary Pemberton said the TAB could only expand if the State's racing industry became more performance-oriented, and expanded its business. Pemberton cautioned that it would be too radical to corporatise racing and warned against comparing the NSW TAB to Victoria's successful Tabcorp Holdings Ltd. Page 21.

Kimberley Resources Ltd has recovered a further eight diamonds from its Blina diamond prospect in the Kimberley region of Western Australia. Blina's Pit 5 area has now yielded 33 diamonds weighing a total of 14.46 carats. Company chairman Miles Kennedy sad Kimberley's prime focus this year was a 10,000-tonne bulk sample program aimed at finding undiscovered lamproite pipes in the area. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Qantas chairman Gary Pemberton, who will be chairman of the board to oversee the Totalisator Agency Board after its A$1.5 billion privatisation later this year, has flagged an expansion of the racing industry in NSW. Pemberton indicated an expansion wouldbe based on greater funding, regular Sunday racing and revamped club membership structures. Page 17.

CanWest Global Communications overall 32 per cent jump in broadcasting operating profit was helped by a A$94.2 million contribution from the Ten Network, a 35 per cent increase in the nine months to May 31. The rise reflects CanWest's 76 per cent economic interest in Ten. Page 17.

Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade figures released yesterday show international gold sales by Australian producers rose five per cent in 1996 to A$5.5 billion - higher than all other commodities except coal. The Department had forecast that gold export volumes would remain flat. Page 17.

Rating agency Standard & Poor analyst Michael Wilkins yesterday said high debt levels could be trouble for the deregulating Victorian power industry. Wilkins said that privatising part of the power industry had led to debt levels higher than elsewhere and that companies with high gearing would have a difficult time servicing debt. Page 18.

Letters of intent for iron ore contracts from diversified miner North's A$1.3 billion West Angelas project in Western Australia are expected to be signed by Japanese steel mills in September. North will begin the process of applying for environmental apprval with newspaper advertisements next weekend. Page 21.

Leading economist Fred Argy has claimed A$14 billion of proposed private sector infrastructure projects was being impeded by the Queensland Government. Argy made his claims in a report commissioned by the Infrastructure Association of Queensland. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Entertainment group Village Roadshow is looking to sell up to 10 stand-alone cinema sites it owns or part-owns in Sydney and Melbourne in a A$200 million listed property trust. The proposal is to help fund aggressive expansion plans and to take its Australian cinemas off the balance sheet. Page 37.

The most successful Australian empire builder, David Johnson, has been named Director of the Year in the United States. Starting without an inheritance, Johnson has helped build more than A$20 billion in stock market wealth and around A$100 million in net personal worth, mostly from stock options. Page 37.

CanWest Global Communications will take on the Federal Government in the Federal Court today in two separate actions against the Australian Broadcasting Authority and Federal Treasurer Peter Costello, who could be called to give evidence. Page 37.

Trustee Corporations Association of Australia president Graham Bradley yesterday described as "mischievous" demands from some fund manager organisations that recommendations on superannuation and collective investments contained in the Wallis report be imlemented urgently. Page 40.

Some independent grocers in Victoria that now buy from Davids and Coles Myer are believed to be negotiating with Woolworths as it opens its new A$250 million independent grocery business in the State. Davids is already struggling under fierce competition from longer trading hours in the State. Page 39.

Melbourne multimedia company Empire Ridge has collapsed, and the Australian Securities Commission may investigate possible breaches by the company's directors of the Corporations Law for trading while insolvent. Page 41.
THE AGE

The Federal Government's prediction of strong economic recovery in the new financial year has been endorsed by market economists, with jobs and output predicted to increase in the next 12 months. Economists expect gross domestic product to grow 3.8 per cet and employment to grow by 2.3 per cent, creating almost 200,000 jobs, but predict the unemployment rate to be 8.3 per cent in June 1998. Page B1.

Standard and Poor analyst Michael Wilkins yesterday criticised the newly privatised Victorian power industry's high levels of debt and the creation of unrealistically low spot prices, calling the situation a "recipe for disaster". Wilkins' comments followrumours that one generator was attempting to renegotiate the terms of its debt facilities. Page B1.

Entertainment group Village Roadshow is looking to spin-off a A$200-million listed property trust in the third big capital raising venture by the group since April last year. The proposal, which is still in its early stages, may offer a distribution yield of around eight per cent. Page B1.

Retail investors who bought ICI Australia stock at A$11.95 a piece in its A$2.2 billion stock sale are expected to reap a big profit of an expected 75 cents a share when the shares begin trading today. Page B3.

The Industry Commission's draft report recommending cuts in the tariffs protecting textile, footwear and clothing has knocked the confidence of knitting mill owner Bill Delaconte, who has put all new investment on hold. Delaconte has met about 40 other loal businessmen from the industry to discuss the problem. Page B3.

Empire Ridge, the multimedia company which pioneered multimedia graphic arts, printing and distribution, and whose annual turnover grew 561 per cent between 1992 and 1996, has gone bust. The company was placed into liquidation on 23 June and its finances are still under examination. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
